video_caption: The video segment opens with a light grey gradient background featuring a logo in the center. The logo depicts two cartoon-style figures, a boy and a girl, with black hair and simple bodies (blue top for the boy, pink for the girl), holding an open, red-covered book between them, their arms raised in a cheerful gesture. Below the figures, the text "YesLearners" is displayed in brown, and beneath that, "you are learning..." in smaller, darker text. A white YouTube logo on a red background is visible in the bottom left corner. The scene then transitions at 00:08 to display a large, dark blue rounded rectangle in the center, containing the white text "Vitamins". In the top right corner, a smaller version of the "YesLearners" logo is shown, along with the text "YesLearners" and "www.yeslearners.com" below it. A male voice-over begins, stating, "Hi friends, in this video we are going to study about vitamins. This video will be useful for all competitive exams conducted by UPSC, SSC, IBPS, and all other public service commissions." At 00:23, the scene changes again. The background remains a light grey gradient, but now large red text that says "SUBSCRIBE" appears at the top. Below this, there's an image with a red-to-orange gradient background. On the left side of this image, a screenshot shows a YouTube "Subscribed" button with a checkmark and a bell icon, overlaid with white text "Click Bell". On the right side of the image is a 3D-rendered "You Tube" logo. The "YesLearners" logo and website address are still present in the top right corner. The voice-over continues, saying, "For more videos".

The video presents information about vitamins, starting with a screen displaying "Vitamins" at the top left. Below it are two black and white portraits: on the left, a man with a mustache, identified by the text "Frederick Hopkins" in a yellow box, and on the right, another man, identified by "Kazimierz Funk" in a blue box. The audio states that vitamins were discovered by Frederick Hopkins and the term "Vitamin" was given by Kazimierz Funk. The next scene categorizes vitamins into "Fat Soluble Vitamins A, D, E, K" (in an orange box) and "Water Soluble Vitamins B, C" (in a green box). Following this, a slide focuses on "Vitamin A1", identifying its scientific name as "Retinol" (in a blue box) and its deficiency disease as "Night Blindness" (in an orange box), accompanied by an image of a dimly lit street with car headlights. "Vitamin A2" is then presented, with its scientific name "Dehydro Retinol" (in a yellow box) and deficiency disease "Xerophthalmia" (in a green box), along with an image of a red, inflamed eye. The next screen displays "Vitamin A" at the top, showing images of carrots, an assortment of green leafy vegetables, a close-up of a human eye with long eyelashes, and a glass of milk, illustrating sources and the organ it benefits. Finally, "Pro Vitamin A" is highlighted, with "Beta Carotene" in a yellow box, and an image below it displays various orange-colored foods like carrots, oranges, papaya, and squash, emphasizing sources rich in beta carotene. The last segment covers "Vitamin D," naming its scientific name as "Calciferol" (in an orange box), and its deficiency diseases "Rickets" (in a green box) and "Osteomalacia" (in a blue box), with corresponding images of a child's bowed legs (Rickets) and a human spine with an abnormal curvature (Osteomalacia).

The video segment presents information about vitamins D, E, and K, their scientific names, and associated deficiencies. From 0:01 to 0:16, the screen displays "Vitamin D" and its scientific name "Calciferol," with "Rickets" and "Osteomalacia" listed below. Under "Rickets," there is an image of two boys with bowed legs, and under "Osteomalacia," there's an anatomical drawing of a human spine. A female voice explains that Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults, affecting bones. From 0:16 to 0:24, the text changes to "Osteoporosis," "porous bone," and "Deficiency of Calcium." Three images show magnified bone cross-sections with increasing porosity from left to right. The voice notes that osteoporosis affects bones due to calcium deficiency. From 0:24 to 0:43, the screen shows "Vitamin D" again, along with alternative names: "Sunshine Vitamin," "Anti Ricketic Vitamin," and "Steroid Vitamin," accompanied by a winking sun icon. The voice explains that Vitamin D is absent in vegetables but produced in the body by ultraviolet rays. From 0:43 to 1:14, the focus shifts to "Vitamin E," labeled "Tocopherol." "Sterility" is shown below, with a cartoon image of a family (father, mother holding a baby) on the left. At 0:53, an image of broken eggshells with yellow yolks appears on the right. The voice identifies Tocopherol as Vitamin E's scientific name, stating its deficiency causes infertility or sterility. It's also called "Beauty Vitamin" and "Sterility Vitamin," essential for reproductive functions, and abundant in egg yolk. Finally, from 1:14 to 1:19, the screen displays "Vitamin K" and its scientific name "Phylloquinone," with "Coagulation Vitamin" and "Haemophilia" listed. A graphic showing a blood vessel with blood cells and a splashing blood drop illustrates blood clotting. The voice identifies Phylloquinone as the scientific name for Vitamin K. Throughout the video, a "YesLearners" logo is visible in the top right corner.

The video segment presents a static educational slide against a light gray background. At the top center, a white rectangular box with a black border displays the text "Vitamin K". Below this, a green rectangular box shows "Phylloquinone". In the middle, an orange rectangular box contains the text "Coagulation Vitamin". At the bottom, a yellow rectangular box features the text "Haemophilia". To the right, an illustration depicts a reddish-brown tube, likely a blood vessel, from which a large quantity of bright red liquid, representing blood, is vigorously splashing out against a white background. In the top right corner, a small logo showcases two cartoon figures holding an open book, with the white text "YesLearners" and "www.yeslearners.com" underneath.

The video displays information about vitamins B1 and B2 on a light grey background. From 0:01, the screen focuses on Vitamin B1. A white box at the top reads "Vitamin B1". Below it, a green box contains "Thiamine", and a yellow box below that reads "Beriberi". On the left, a collage of various food items like whole grain bread, eggs, cereals, rice, dry beans, and peanuts is shown, labeled "GROUP OF FOODS RICH IN VITAMIN B." On the right, an image depicts two hands with red, spotted skin, captioned "Beriberi Disease". A female voice explains that Vitamin B1 is Thiamine, and its deficiency causes Beriberi, which affects the human nervous system. From 0:16, the screen transitions to Vitamin B2, with "Vitamin B2" in a white box at the top. A green box below it shows "Riboflavin", and a yellow box at the bottom says "Ariboflavinosis". To the right, a close-up image of a person's severely chapped and irritated lips is presented. The voiceover states that the scientific name of Vitamin B2 is Riboflavin, and its deficiency causes Ariboflavinosis. At 0:29, the green box changes to "Protein Synthesis", and the yellow box to "Yellow colour of milk". The voice explains that Vitamin B2 is essential for protein synthesis and gives milk its pale yellow color. It further notes that Vitamin B2 is lost if milk is exposed to sunlight for a long time. Throughout the video, a small "YesLearners" logo with a website address is visible in the top right corner.

The video displays a white screen with a grey background, featuring several text boxes and an image. At the top, a black box contains the white text "Vitamin B 3". Directly below it, a green box shows the white text "Niacin or Nicotinic Acid", which is being spoken in the audio. Further down, a yellow box with black text reads "Pellagra", and underneath it, an orange box has the black text "4 D Syndrome". To the right of these text boxes, an image depicts two hands with a severe, reddish, and scaly rash, indicating a skin condition. In the top right corner, a logo for "YesLearners" (www.yeslearners.com) is visible, showing two cartoon figures reading books.

The video opens with a light grey background and displays the text "Vitamin C" at the top. Below it, in a green horizontal bar, is "Ascorbic Acid" (English), followed by "Scurvy" (English) in a yellow bar, and "Sailors plague" (English) in an orange bar at the bottom. The "YesLearners" logo, featuring two cartoon people reading a book and the website "www.yeslearners.com," is visible in the top right corner throughout this segment. At 0:16, the text in the green bar changes to "Fresh food vitamin" (English), and the text in the orange bar changes to "Anti cancer vitamin" (English). Simultaneously, two images appear on the left side of the screen: a collage of various fruits like oranges, lemons, pineapple, and strawberries in the top left, and a close-up of green gooseberries on a branch in the bottom left. A circular icon with "vitamin c" (English) is also part of the fruit collage. A female voice narrates the information displayed on screen. At 0:58, the screen transitions to a solid purple color, and then at 0:59, it changes to a white background with a green play button icon and the text "thanks for watching" (English).

The video segment features a static teal-colored background. In the center, white text reads "and don't forget to SUBSCRIBE", with "SUBSCRIBE" in a larger, bold font and enclosed within a white rectangular outline. At 0:06, a purple rectangular button appears directly below this text, displaying "www.yeslearners.com" in white text. All text and the button remain stationary for the remainder of the segment.
